title: Front Seat Control Switch
introduction:
The seat control switch mounts behind the seat’s outer side shield. Think of that shield as a tiny dashboard: it carries the controls and their electrical connection, so its release sequence matters. I locate the handle clip and screws before moving the trim—this is a puzzle, not a tug-of-war.

I cover removal, refitting and an ordinary check of the fitted power-seat controls. The elongated switch moves the seat cushion; the separate round lumbar control is not the part removed here. This is not electrical fault isolation.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. Review the applicable [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning.

items.name: Protect yourself
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use this protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Trim removal tool
items.detail: Have the trim removal tool illustrated beside the switch knob available, along with tools that fit the shield and switch screws. Tool sizes are not specified.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustrations show the LHD driver seat. The procedure is similar for the other seats.
edits.why: I use the pictured seat as an attachment map, allowing for the different side and orientation of the seat being serviced.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they may also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The removal and refitting instructions belong together, even where a detail appears under removal.

edits.text: Release the retaining clip around the front seat recline handle’s hub, moving it sideways in the direction of the illustrated arrow. Remove the handle from its shaft.
edits.why: The enlarged view shows the clip around the handle’s central opening. Freeing that retainer allows the handle to come off without using the surrounding shield as a lever.

edits.text: Remove the side shield screws at the lower attachment locations shown in the front and rear views.
edits.why: I check both views before moving the shield: the rear attachment is tucked behind the trim and is easy to overlook.

edits.text: Remove the side shield using the following release and disconnection sequence.
edits.why: The shield carries the switch connection. Free the trim in the stated order before separating it from the wiring.

edits.text: Lift the rear of the side shield upward, then pull that rear section outward, away from the seat.
edits.why: This releases the rear section beside the recline-handle opening before the shield moves along the seat.

edits.text: Push the side shield forward, toward the front of the seat.
edits.why: This is a separate movement after lifting and pulling the rear outward. The shield has a release sequence, rather than one all-purpose tug.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector on the back of the side shield, then separate the shield from the seat.
edits.why: The inset locates the connection behind the control area. Disconnecting it frees the shield without leaving it hanging from the harness.

edits.text: Use the illustrated trim removal tool to ease the elongated seat control switch knob off the switch.
edits.why: The highlighted part is the elongated knob beside the round control. Removing it clears the outer face of the switch before the switch body comes out from behind.

edits.text: From the inside of the removed side shield, remove the screws around the seat control switch and lift the switch out of the shield.
edits.why: The rear view identifies the switch body and its highlighted mounting screws, helping distinguish them from the shield’s other molded features.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order: fit the switch into the side shield and install its screws, then refit the switch knob. Reconnect the electrical connector. Move the shield rearward to reverse its forward release movement, then return its rear section inward and downward into position. Install the side shield screws, then refit the recline handle with its retaining clip engaged.
edits.why: Working backward through the release movements restores the shield’s position and reconnects the control before the trim is secured. Check that the connector, knob and handle retainer are seated. Once the switch, shield and recline handle are completely refitted, clear tools, people and objects from the seat’s travel, including behind the backrest. Keep the car stationary, the parking brake applied and the parked gear selected; never adjust the driver seat while moving. Use the elongated outboard switch to move the seat forward and backward, and move its front or rear end up and down to check the fitted cushion adjustments shown in the [owner’s power-seat controls](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539512&Uid=G1634988&ProcUid=G1638641&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web). Use short movements with room available; do not treat the separate round lumbar knob as this switch. If ignition power is needed, bring the valid key inside and, from confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP with both pedals released for engine-off ON; if already ON, leave it ON. Check that the seat responds in the requested directions, then return it to a comfortable driving position with everyone clear. Return any known ON state to OFF by pressing and releasing START/STOP without pressing either pedal; leave an already-OFF state alone. With the ignition OFF, remove the key before any connector or trim reinspection. If a fitted movement does not work or the trim interferes, stop and resolve it before driving. This is a normal operation check, not proof of an isolated electrical diagnosis.

editorialRevision.scope: Known-state stationary setup, owner-backed fitted power-seat movement and final OFF; all primary mechanical action text unchanged. Increment pending independent review.
